## 1. Introduction

The study of the structure of the universe is one of the most fundamental problems in physics. The large-scale structure of the universe, including galaxies, clusters of galaxies, and superclusters, has been shaped by gravitational interactions over billions of years. Understanding this structure provides insights into the initial conditions of the universe, the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and the overall evolution of cosmic structures.

One of the key tools for studying the large-scale structure of the universe is the correlation function, which quantifies the statistical relationship between the positions of galaxies or other astronomical objects. The two-point correlation function, in particular, is widely used because it captures the basic clustering properties of matter in the universe. It is defined as the excess probability of finding a pair of galaxies separated by a given distance compared to what would be expected if the galaxies were distributed randomly.

In recent years, there has been significant progress in both theoretical models and observational data for understanding the large-scale structure of the universe. Advances in computational power have allowed for more detailed simulations of structure formation, while new surveys such as the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the Dark Energy Survey (DES) have provided vast amounts of data on galaxy distributions. These developments have enabled researchers to test various cosmological models and refine our understanding of the universe's composition and evolution.

This paper aims to review the current state of knowledge regarding the large-scale structure of the universe, focusing on the two-point correlation function and its implications for cosmology. We will discuss the theoretical foundations of structure formation, the role of dark matter and dark energy, and the latest observational results. Additionally, we will explore the challenges and future directions in this field, highlighting the importance of continued research in unraveling the mysteries of the cosmos.
